sents.d: Protecting capital matters more than any entry signal.
New traders often focus heavily on finding the 'right' strategy while ignoring risk management, but most trading failures come from position sizing and risk control, not strategy choice.

scenes.heading: Risk a small share per trade

sents.d: A common general principle is risking only a small percentage of total capital on any single trade, so that a string of losses doesn't wipe out the account.
Many traders also use predefined stop-loss levels decided before entering a trade, not adjusted emotionally after entering.

This is general education, not financial advice — risk tolerance and appropriate position sizing vary by individual circumstances, and it's worth discussing with a licensed financial professional before trading with real capital.

take: Manage risk first: small position sizes protect the account.
